newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA WIN SPANISH CUP FOR 23RD TIME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA WIN SPANISH CUP FOR 23RD TIME.

text.p: Portuguese international Luis Figo was Barcelona's hero in their extra-time 3-2 Spanish Cup final victory against Real Betis at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium in Madrid on Saturday.
Figo scored the decisive goal five minutes from the end of extra time to give the Catalan club a record equalling 23rd Cup victory.
They now have the same number of Cup wins as Athletic Bilbao.
The victory brought a triumphant end to Bobby Robson's year as Barcelona's coach.
Robson has another year left on his contract with the club but he has already said he will not stay on in his present role.
The former England manager has been under pressure from Barcelona fans and the media throughout the season.
Despite Barcelona lifting the Cup, to add to the Cup Winners' Cup and a second place finish in the Spanish league, Robson's critics may still find much to complain about.
Barcelona were second best for much of the match and had to come from behind twice.
Betis took the initiative from the start and their early efforts quickly paid off.
Alfonso Munoz, wearing the number eleven shirt, scored in the 11th minute.
The Spanish international striker swept past two Barcelona players down the right wing but a weak shot ricocheted off Barcelona defender Albert Ferrer.
Alfonso managed to get a second touch and the ball spun round the luckless Ferrer and a despondent Vitor Baia in the Barcelona goal.
Brutal tackles marked most of the first half but only a few players were shown the yellow card.
Betis defender Albert Nadj was booked in the 13th minute after bringing down Figo.
Figo himself was booked for a similar challenge on Roberto Rios after 43 minutes.
He quickly redeemed himself with the first of his important interventions in the direction of the game.
A minute before half-time he got his foot to the ball in a penalty area melee and slotted it past Pedro Jaro in the Betis goal to make the score 1-1 at the break.
Both sides started cautiously in the second half and there were few further chances until the 77th minute when Juan Urena clumsily challenged Luis Enrique in the penalty area as he was clear on goal.
However Barcelona claims for a penalty were ignored.

The game seemed to be ebbing towards extra time when a pass from Alfonso let Nigerian international Finidi George slide onto the ball on the right hand side of the box and put it beyond the reach of Vitor Baia.
Betis celebrations were premature though because their concentration lapsed as Tomas Olias came on for Nadj and Barcelona striker Juan Pizzi scored almost immediately at the other end.
During extra time both sides tried to play creative soccer to find an opening but seemed too tired to make the decisive move until Figo found some energy.
Running through the middle he found Oscar Garcia out wide on the left.
The substitute's shot fell conveniently at the feet of Figo for his second goal.

Barcelona: Vitor Baia, Albert Ferrer (Oscar Garcia 91), Abdelardo Fernandez, Fernando Couto, Sergi Barjuan, Josep Guardiola, Luis Figo, Hristo Stoichkov (Emmanuel Ammunike 72), Ivan de la Pena (Gheorge Popescu 100), Luis Enrique, Juan Pizzi.

Real Betis: Pedro Jaro, Jaime Quesada, Albert Nadj (Tomas Olias 85), Hristo Vidakovic, Roberto Rios, Juan Merino, (Juan Urena 70) Alexis Trujillo, Juan Canas (Pier Cherubino 77), Robert Jarni, Finidi George, Alfonso Munoz.
